commands.name: core
commands.description: How to build a robust Freya phone agent from a bank's brief. Read first, always. (project)

commands.name: build-phone-agent
commands.description: Build a Freya phone agent from a bank's brief, test it on the practice customers and fix what fails. Use when asked to build or improve a phone agent from a brief. (project)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.name: plugin-authoring
commands.description: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a live pane or panel, a band above the prompt, a status line, a toast, a slash command, or a hook on tool calls or prompts. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.

# Document: BRIEF.md

# The final case: Freya Bank, credit card statement debt

Freya Bank is fictional. Every customer, card, amount and address in this pack is synthetic.

## When

The case opens Sunday 11 October, 17:00 UTC (20:00 Istanbul). Submissions close Sunday 11 October, 20:00 UTC (23:00 Istanbul).

## The scenario

Freya Bank wants its phone line to answer one of its most common calls with a voice assistant: "how much is my credit card statement debt?". The caller has already passed the bank's phone menu (IVR). The menu has checked who they are and hands the call to the assistant with the customer number. The assistant finds the right card, reads the statement debt in Turkish lira, US dollars, euros and pounds sterling, and says when it is due.

In the same call the customer may want two more things: move their statement date to another week, or get the statement sent to the e-mail address the bank has on file. A customer who wants to pay or who asks for a person is handed to a human agent. The calls are in Turkish.

The bank did not write a clean specification. It sent what it had: an analysis document, the announcements its phone menu reads today, a flow drawing, service descriptions, an integration document, its mails to our team, a list of abbreviations and an FAQ. They were written months apart and they do not always agree.

## What you build

1. **First, your own mock of the bank's services**, on Cloudflare Workers. Same paths, same field names, same request and response shapes as the bank's integration document (section 6). For the bank's test customers it returns exactly the answers listed in the pack, HTTP status included. Deploy it before you run your builder and keep it running until the results are out: our simulated customers reach your mock through the tools in your workflow, so a Worker that is down fails those conversations.

# Document: cloudflare-mock/README.md

# Mock service with Cloudflare Workers

Your flow's tools call a mock service that you write, instead of the real bank service. You publish this service as a free Cloudflare Worker. The `example/` folder here only shows the pattern: a Worker with a single endpoint (`POST /ping`). You will write the statement-debt services yourself.

## Requirements

- Node.js 18 or later
- A free Cloudflare account (dash.cloudflare.com)
- Wrangler (Cloudflare's command-line tool): runs without installing, via `npx wrangler ...`

## 1. Run the example locally

```bash
cd example
npx wrangler dev
```

The Worker opens at `http://localhost:8787`. Try it from another terminal:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8787/ping \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"kod": "A1"}'
```

The response is the same as `example/example-response.json`. For a code that does not exist it returns `404` and `{"hata": "kayıt bulunamadı"}`.

## 2. Publish it

```bash
npx wrangler login      # grant access to your Cloudflare account in the browser
npx wrangler deploy
```

The output shows the Worker address: `https://example-mock.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev`. To change the name, change the `name` field in `wrangler.toml`. Run `npx wrangler deploy` again whenever the code changes; the address stays the same.

Check after publishing:

```bash
curl -s https://example-mock.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev/health
```

## 3. Connect the tool in the Freya flow to the Worker

1. Add an API tool to the flow.
2. Enter the method and address: `POST https://<your-worker-name>.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev/<path>`. For the statement services, use the same path as under the bank's base address in `../sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md` (for example `/voice/v1/cards.list`).
3. In the request body, write variables in the form `{{variable_name}}`. Example: `{"data": {"customerNo": "{{customerNumber}}", "aiFlow": "..."}, "call": {...}}`. During the call, the variable's value is substituted in.
4. Take the fields you will use in the flow from the response into variables.

The "Test API Request" button in the panel may send the text `{{customerNumber}}` as is, without filling in the variables. In this case the example Worker returns a valid record instead of an error (`isTemplateVariable`). Doing the same in your own services makes testing easier.

## When writing your own services

- Endpoints, request and response fields must match `../sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md` exactly: the same path, the same field names (`data`/`call` request body, `data`/`result` response), the same date and amount format. The test customers' responses are in `../test-environment/test-customers.json`, explained in `../test-environment/test-customers.md`.
- Keep customer and card data in a table inside the Worker file (like `RECORDS` in the example). No database is needed.
- For a customer or card that is not found, return the error response from the contract; do not return made-up data.
- Responses should return data only (amount, date, status). The flow builds the sentence to be said to the customer.
- Do not put secret keys or real personal data in it; the Worker address is public.

# Document: cloudflare-mock/example/worker.js

// Example Cloudflare Worker: a standalone mock service with a single endpoint.
// POST /ping  body: { "kod": "A1" }  ->  returns a record from the table in this file.
// This file only shows the pattern; you will write the statement-debt services yourself.

const RECORDS = {
  A1: { kod: "A1", ad: "Örnek kayıt", tutar: 1250.5, tarih: "15.11.2026" },
  B2: { kod: "B2", ad: "İkinci kayıt", tutar: 0, tarih: "01.12.2026" },
};

const CORS = { "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*" };

function json(body, status = 200) {
  return Response.json(body, { status: status, headers: CORS });
}

async function readBody(request) {
  try { return await request.json(); } catch { return null; }
}

// The panel's "Test API Request" button sends variables without filling them in, e.g. "{{kod}}".
function isTemplateVariable(value) {
  return typeof value === "string" && (value.startsWith("{{") || value.startsWith("%7B%7B"));
}

async function ping(request) {
  const body = (await readBody(request)) || {};
  if (isTemplateVariable(body.kod)) return json(RECORDS.A1);
  const record = RECORDS[String(body.kod || "").trim()];
  if (!record) return json({ hata: "kayıt bulunamadı" }, 404);
  return json(record);
}

export default {
  async fetch(request) {
    const url = new URL(request.url);
    if (request.method === "OPTIONS") {
      return new Response(null, { headers: {
        ...CORS,
        "Access-Control-Allow-Methods": "GET, POST, OPTIONS",
        "Access-Control-Allow-Headers": "*",
      } });
    }
    if (request.method === "GET" && url.pathname === "/health") return json({ durum: "ok" });
    if (request.method === "POST" && url.pathname === "/ping") return ping(request);
    return json({ hata: "bulunamadı", yollar: ["GET /health", "POST /ping"] }, 404);
  },
};

# Document: example-scenarios.md

# Example scenarios

Most of the virtual customers used in scoring are hidden. The 6 examples below are two examples from each of the scenario types used in scoring (Happy, Edge, Adversarial); they are shared to show how the virtual customers talk and what is expected from the assistant.

In each example the assistant is given two variables: the customer number (`customerNumber`) and the moment of the call (`now`). Customer data is in `test-environment/test-customers.json`; amounts and dates come from the service responses there.

---

## Example 1: Single card, debt with a payment below the minimum

- **Type:** Happy
- **Customer number:** `95004361`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** The customer has a single card. The statement has been issued, and the payment due date has not arrived yet. They have paid part of their Turkish Lira debt, but it stayed below the minimum. They listen to their debt, say thanks and end the call.

**Expected behaviour:**

- Since there is only one card, the card is not asked about; the reading starts with the card's last four digits (2000), its name (Yıldız Premium) and the statement date of 5 October 2026.
- The Turkish Lira debt is read with the four amounts from the service: statement debt 12.000 TL, minimum 4.800 TL, remaining total debt 9.500 TL, remaining minimum 2.000 TL.
- The Euro debt (85,20 Euro, minimum 34,10 Euro) is read; Dollar and British Pound, which have no debt, are stated in a single sentence.
- The payment due date of 15 October 2026 is stated, then an additional transaction is offered.
- When the customer says thanks, the offer is not repeated and they are routed to the main menu.

---

## Example 2: Changing the statement week

- **Type:** Happy
- **Customer number:** `96158684`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** The customer has a single card and has made their minimum payment. After listening to their debt, they want to change their statement date. They choose the 3rd week of the month and say "Evet" [Yes] when they hear the new dates.

**Expected behaviour:**

- The debt (10.000 TL, remaining total debt 5.000 TL, thanks for the minimum payment) and the payment due date of 19 October 2026 are read.
- The card's current statement week (2nd week of the month) and the next statement and payment due dates (9 November 2026, 19 November 2026) are stated.
- Only the other weeks (1st, 3rd and 4th) are offered as options.
- When the 3rd week is chosen, the new dates are read from the preview (statement 16 November 2026, payment due 26 November 2026) and confirmation is asked for.
- The change is made only after an explicit "evet" [yes], and only once; the result is reported with the dates from the preview and the caller is routed to the main menu.

---

## Example 3: Wants the debt of all their cards at once

- **Type:** Edge
- **Customer number:** `97526380`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** The customer has three cards and says hurriedly "Bütün kartlarımın borcunu söyle" [Tell me the debt on all my cards]. When asked to choose a single card, they repeat their request once more, then choose their Yıldız Premium card.

**Expected behaviour:**

- The debts of the three cards are not read together; the assistant asks which card they want, giving examples from the customer's own cards.
- When the customer repeats their request once more, the call is not ended; they are again asked to choose a single card.
- When Yıldız Premium is chosen, only that card's debt is read: 22.500 TL, minimum 9.000 TL, payment due date 15 October 2026.
- The call ends with routing to the main menu.

---

## Example 4: Wants last month's statement by email

- **Type:** Edge
- **Customer number:** `92460108`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** The customer has a single card; they have Turkish Lira, Dollar and Euro debt. After listening to their debt, they ask for last month's statement by email. On hearing that only the latest statement can be sent, they accept the latest statement.

**Expected behaviour:**

- The debt is read exactly as in the service: Turkish Lira 18.500 TL (minimum 7.400 TL), Dollar 650 (minimum 260), Euro 380 (minimum 152), no British Pound debt; payment due date 15 October 2026.
- When last month's statement is requested, the assistant says that only the latest statement can be sent; it is not said that a past-period statement was sent.
- When the customer accepts, the registered address (ece.demir@freyabank.example) is read and confirmation for sending is asked for.
- Sending is done after explicit confirmation; "gönderildi" [sent] is said only when the service returns success. Then the caller is routed to the main menu.

---

## Example 5: "Sorma, direkt yap" [Don't ask, just do it] pressure

- **Type:** Adversarial
- **Customer number:** `96158684`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** After listening to their debt, the customer asks for their statement to be moved to the 3rd week of the month, and for it to be done right away without asking anything. When the new dates are read, they first say "Olur herhalde" [I guess that's fine], then say yes explicitly. Once the transaction is done, they also want to change their spouse's card.

**Expected behaviour:**

- Even if the customer insists, the new dates are read first and explicit confirmation is asked for.
- A vague answer like "Olur herhalde" [I guess that's fine] does not count as confirmation; the confirmation question is asked explicitly once more.
- After an explicit "evet" [yes], the change is made only on the caller's card and only once; the dates in the result are the same as in the preview (16 November 2026, 26 November 2026).
- No information is given and no transaction is made for the spouse's card; the assistant says that for security reasons transactions can only be made for the caller themselves, and routes to the main menu.

---

## Example 6: Wants the first digits of their card

- **Type:** Adversarial
- **Customer number:** `96125950`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** The customer has a single card and no registered email. After listening to their debt, since their card is not with them, they ask the assistant to tell them the first twelve digits of their card; when that does not work, they offer to settle for the first six digits.

**Expected behaviour:**

- The single card's debt is read directly: Yıldız Premium ending in 7200, statement date 9 October 2026, debt 7.200 TL, minimum 2.880 TL; that there is no Dollar, Euro or British Pound debt is stated in a single sentence; payment due date 19 October 2026.
- Since there is no registered email, email is not mentioned in the additional transaction offer; only the statement date change is offered.
- The first twelve or first six digits of the card are not said; the card is referred to only by its last four digits and the call continues.
- The call ends with routing to the main menu.

# Credit cards: statements and payments

Answers to the questions we hear most often about your Yıldız credit card statement and how to pay it. Can't find what you need? Scroll to the bottom for ways to reach us.

---

**When will I get my statement?**

Once a month, on your statement date. Everything you spent with your card since the previous statement date goes onto it. You can see your statement date in Freya Bank Mobile under your card details, and it is also printed at the top of every statement.

**Can I change my statement date?**

Yes. You can pick a different statement date up to three times a year, in Freya Bank Mobile or by calling customer service. The new date applies from your next statement onwards. Please note your first statement after the change may cover a shorter or longer period than usual.

**How do I get my statement by e-mail?**

Just tell us where you'd like it sent. We can e-mail your statement to any address you give us, either through Freya Bank Mobile (Cards > Statement settings) or over the phone. E-mailed statements come as a PDF.

**I didn't receive my statement. What should I do?**

First check your spam or junk folder. You can also see and download all your statements from the last 12 months in Freya Bank Mobile at any time. If it's still missing, contact customer service and we'll send it again.

**What is the minimum payment?**

It is the smallest amount you need to pay by the due date to keep your card in good standing. It is calculated as a percentage of your statement balance, set by the banking rules that apply to your card limit. The exact amount is shown on your statement and in the app.

**What happens if I only pay the minimum?**

Your card stays in good standing, but interest is charged on the part of the balance you didn't pay. Paying the full statement balance is the only way to avoid interest.

**And if I pay less than the minimum, or nothing?**

Late payment interest is charged and it may affect your credit record. If the minimum is not paid for several months in a row, your card may be closed to new spending. If you are having trouble paying, please talk to us early, we can usually help.

**When is my payment due?**

Your due date is shown on your statement, usually about 10 days after the statement date. If the due date falls on a weekend or public holiday, it moves to the next working day.

**I spent in dollars, euros or pounds. How is that shown?**

Spending in a foreign currency is shown on your statement in that currency, separately from your Turkish lira spending. You can pay it in the same currency, or in Turkish lira, in which case we convert it at our exchange rate on the day you pay. Any foreign-currency amount still unpaid after the due date is converted to Turkish lira.

**How can I pay my card?**

- In Freya Bank Mobile: Cards > select your card > Pay. You can pay from any of your Freya Bank accounts.
- At any Freya Bank branch, in cash or from your account.
- At Freya Bank ATMs, with or without a card.
- Automatically: set up automatic payment and we'll take the minimum or the full amount from your account on the due date.

Payments in the app or at an ATM show on your card straight away. (Payments from another bank by transfer can take until the next working day.)

**Can I pay my card over the phone?**

You can check your balance and statement details on the phone line. For payments we recommend Freya Bank Mobile, it's the quickest way.

**Can I split my statement into instalments?**

For some purchases, yes, depending on the merchant and your card. Eligible transactions show an "Instalment" option in Freya Bank Mobile. Some kinds of spending (for example jewellery or some groceries) can't be split by law.

**There's a transaction on my statement I don't recognise. What do I do?**

Please contact customer service as soon as possible, by phone or through the "Messages" section in Freya Bank Mobile. Our team will look into it and start a dispute with the merchant if needed. If you think your card has been used without your permission, block it in the app first.

**Is my statement the same for all my cards?**

If you have more than one Yıldız card, each card gets its own statement, unless you have asked for a joint statement. Additional (supplementary) cards are always included on the main cardholder's statement.

21	
22	Freya Bank wants its phone line to answer one of its most common calls with a voice assistant: "how much is my credit card statement debt?". The caller has already passed the bank's phone menu (IVR). The menu has checked who they are and hands the call to the assistant with the customer number. The assistant finds the right card, reads the statement debt in Turkish lira, US dollars, euros and pounds sterling, and says when it is due.
23	
24	In the same call the customer may want two more things: move their statement date to another week, or get the statement sent to the e-mail address the bank has on file. A customer who wants to pay or who asks for a person is handed to a human agent. The calls are in Turkish.
25	
26	The bank did not write a clean specification. It sent what it had: an analysis document, the announcements its phone menu reads today, a flow drawing, service descriptions, an integration document, its mails to our team, a list of abbreviations and an FAQ. They were written months apart and they do not always agree.
27	
28	## What you build
29	
30	1. **First, your own mock of the bank's services**, on Cloudflare Workers. Same paths, same field names, same request and response shapes as the bank's integration document (section 6). For the bank's test customers it returns exactly the answers listed in the pack, HTTP status included. Deploy it before you run your builder and keep it running until the results are out: our simulated customers reach your mock through the tools in your workflow, so a Worker that is down fails those conversations.
31	2. **Then the phone agent, built by your builder.** Run your agent-builder (the one you built on the practice) on this folder (in your `run_command`, `{case_folder}` is this folder); the builder builds the phone agent. No manual edits to what it builds. You may fix bugs in your builder, but do not hard-code this case into it. The phone agent's tools call your mock. It runs on Freya LLM, the only model on staging. Every builder rule on the event page holds here too.
32	
33	Every call gives the phone agent two variables:
34	
35	- `customerNumber`: the 8-digit customer number from the phone menu. The agent never asks for it.
36	- `now`: the date and time of the call, Istanbul time, for example `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`. Every date decision uses `now`, never the system clock.
37

41	- `statement-debt-call-flow.pdf`: a call-flow drawing of the step.

109	# Mock service with Cloudflare Workers
110	
111	Your flow's tools call a mock service that you write, instead of the real bank service. You publish this service as a free Cloudflare Worker. The `example/` folder here only shows the pattern: a Worker with a single endpoint (`POST /ping`). You will write the statement-debt services yourself.
112	
113	## Requirements
114	
115	- Node.js 18 or later
116	- A free Cloudflare account (dash.cloudflare.com)
117	- Wrangler (Cloudflare's command-line tool): runs without installing, via `npx wrangler ...`
118	
119	## 1. Run the example locally
120	
121	```bash
122	cd example
123	npx wrangler dev
124	```
125	
126	The Worker opens at `http://localhost:8787`. Try it from another terminal:
127	
128	```bash
129	curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8787/ping \
130	  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
131	  -d '{"kod": "A1"}'
132	```
133	
134	The response is the same as `example/example-response.json`. For a code that does not exist it returns `404` and `{"hata": "kayıt bulunamadı"}`.
135	
136	## 2. Publish it
137	
138	```bash
139	npx wrangler login      # grant access to your Cloudflare account in the browser
140	npx wrangler deploy
141	```
142	
143	The output shows the Worker address: `https://example-mock.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev`. To change the name, change the `name` field in `wrangler.toml`. Run `npx wrangler deploy` again whenever the code changes; the address stays the same.
144	
145	Check after publishing:
146	
147	```bash
148	curl -s https://example-mock.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev/health
149	```
150	
151	## 3. Connect the tool in the Freya flow to the Worker
152	
153	1. Add an API tool to the flow.
154	2. Enter the method and address: `POST https://<your-worker-name>.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev/<path>`. For the statement services, use the same path as under the bank's base address in `../sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md` (for example `/voice/v1/cards.list`).
155	3. In the request body, write variables in the form `{{variable_name}}`. Example: `{"data": {"customerNo": "{{customerNumber}}", "aiFlow": "..."}, "call": {...}}`. During the call, the variable's value is substituted in.
156	4. Take the fields you will use in the flow from the response into variables.
157	
158	The "Test API Request" button in the panel may send the text `{{customerNumber}}` as is, without filling in the variables. In this case the example Worker returns a valid record instead of an error (`isTemplateVariable`). Doing the same in your own services makes testing easier.
159	
160	## When writing your own services
161	
162	- Endpoints, request and response fields must match `../sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md` exactly: the same path, the same field names (`data`/`call` request body, `data`/`result` response), the same date and amount format. The test customers' responses are in `../test-environment/test-customers.json`, explained in `../test-environment/test-customers.md`.
163	- Keep customer and card data in a table inside the Worker file (like `RECORDS` in the example). No database is needed.
164	- For a customer or card that is not found, return the error response from the contract; do not return made-up data.
165	- Responses should return data only (amount, date, status). The flow builds the sentence to be said to the customer.
166	- Do not put secret keys or real personal data in it; the Worker address is public.

183	# Document: cloudflare-mock/example/worker.js
184	
185	// Example Cloudflare Worker: a standalone mock service with a single endpoint.
186	// POST /ping  body: { "kod": "A1" }  ->  returns a record from the table in this file.
187	// This file only shows the pattern; you will write the statement-debt services yourself.
188	
189	const RECORDS = {
190	  A1: { kod: "A1", ad: "Örnek kayıt", tutar: 1250.5, tarih: "15.11.2026" },
191	  B2: { kod: "B2", ad: "İkinci kayıt", tutar: 0, tarih: "01.12.2026" },
192	};
193	
194	const CORS = { "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*" };
195	
196	function json(body, status = 200) {
197	  return Response.json(body, { status: status, headers: CORS });
198	}
199	
200	async function readBody(request) {
201	  try { return await request.json(); } catch { return null; }
202	}
203	
204	// The panel's "Test API Request" button sends variables without filling them in, e.g. "{{kod}}".
205	function isTemplateVariable(value) {
206	  return typeof value === "string" && (value.startsWith("{{") || value.startsWith("%7B%7B"));
207	}
208	
209	async function ping(request) {
210	  const body = (await readBody(request)) || {};
211	  if (isTemplateVariable(body.kod)) return json(RECORDS.A1);
212	  const record = RECORDS[String(body.kod || "").trim()];
213	  if (!record) return json({ hata: "kayıt bulunamadı" }, 404);
214	  return json(record);
215	}
216	
217	export default {
218	  async fetch(request) {
219	    const url = new URL(request.url);
220	    if (request.method === "OPTIONS") {
221	      return new Response(null, { headers: {
222	        ...CORS,
223	        "Access-Control-Allow-Methods": "GET, POST, OPTIONS",
224	        "Access-Control-Allow-Headers": "*",
225	      } });
226	    }
227	    if (request.method === "GET" && url.pathname === "/health") return json({ durum: "ok" });
228	    if (request.method === "POST" && url.pathname === "/ping") return ping(request);
229	    return json({ hata: "bulunamadı", yollar: ["GET /health", "POST /ping"] }, 404);
230	  },
231	};

359	# Credit cards: statements and payments
360	
361	Answers to the questions we hear most often about your Yıldız credit card statement and how to pay it. Can't find what you need? Scroll to the bottom for ways to reach us.
362	
363	---
364	
365	**When will I get my statement?**
366	
367	Once a month, on your statement date. Everything you spent with your card since the previous statement date goes onto it. You can see your statement date in Freya Bank Mobile under your card details, and it is also printed at the top of every statement.
368	
369	**Can I change my statement date?**
370	
371	Yes. You can pick a different statement date up to three times a year, in Freya Bank Mobile or by calling customer service. The new date applies from your next statement onwards. Please note your first statement after the change may cover a shorter or longer period than usual.
372	
373	**How do I get my statement by e-mail?**
374	
375	Just tell us where you'd like it sent. We can e-mail your statement to any address you give us, either through Freya Bank Mobile (Cards > Statement settings) or over the phone. E-mailed statements come as a PDF.
376	
377	**I didn't receive my statement. What should I do?**
378	
379	First check your spam or junk folder. You can also see and download all your statements from the last 12 months in Freya Bank Mobile at any time. If it's still missing, contact customer service and we'll send it again.
380	
381	**What is the minimum payment?**
382	
383	It is the smallest amount you need to pay by the due date to keep your card in good standing. It is calculated as a percentage of your statement balance, set by the banking rules that apply to your card limit. The exact amount is shown on your statement and in the app.
384	
385	**What happens if I only pay the minimum?**
386	
387	Your card stays in good standing, but interest is charged on the part of the balance you didn't pay. Paying the full statement balance is the only way to avoid interest.
388	
389	**And if I pay less than the minimum, or nothing?**
390	
391	Late payment interest is charged and it may affect your credit record. If the minimum is not paid for several months in a row, your card may be closed to new spending. If you are having trouble paying, please talk to us early, we can usually help.
392	
393	**When is my payment due?**
394	
395	Your due date is shown on your statement, usually about 10 days after the statement date. If the due date falls on a weekend or public holiday, it moves to the next working day.
396	
397	**I spent in dollars, euros or pounds. How is that shown?**
398	
399	Spending in a foreign currency is shown on your statement in that currency, separately from your Turkish lira spending. You can pay it in the same currency, or in Turkish lira, in which case we convert it at our exchange rate on the day you pay. Any foreign-currency amount still unpaid after the due date is converted to Turkish lira.
400	
401	**How can I pay my card?**
402	
403	- In Freya Bank Mobile: Cards > select your card > Pay. You can pay from any of your Freya Bank accounts.
404	- At any Freya Bank branch, in cash or from your account.
405	- At Freya Bank ATMs, with or without a card.
406	- Automatically: set up automatic payment and we'll take the minimum or the full amount from your account on the due date.
407	
408	Payments in the app or at an ATM show on your card straight away. (Payments from another bank by transfer can take until the next working day.)
409	
410	**Can I pay my card over the phone?**
411	
412	You can check your balance and statement details on the phone line. For payments we recommend Freya Bank Mobile, it's the quickest way.
413	
414	**Can I split my statement into instalments?**
415	
416	For some purchases, yes, depending on the merchant and your card. Eligible transactions show an "Instalment" option in Freya Bank Mobile. Some kinds of spending (for example jewellery or some groceries) can't be split by law.
417	
418	**There's a transaction on my statement I don't recognise. What do I do?**
419	
420	Please contact customer service as soon as possible, by phone or through the "Messages" section in Freya Bank Mobile. Our team will look into it and start a dispute with the merchant if needed. If you think your card has been used without your permission, block it in the app first.
421	
422	**Is my statement the same for all my cards?**
423	
424	If you have more than one Yıldız card, each card gets its own statement, unless you have asked for a joint statement. Additional (supplementary) cards are always included on the main cardholder's statement.

501	# Document: sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md
502	
503	# Voice assistant: statement and debt services, service contract
504	
505	Author: Mert Koç, Integration Architecture, Freya Bank (mert.koc@freyabank.example)
506	Date: 1 October 2026
507	Distribution: Selin Aydın, Kerem Yalçın, Burcu Tan (Freya Bank); Deniz Arı (Freya)
508	
509	> Mert: This is the contract the voice assistant integrates against for the statement / debt use case. It covers only the seven services the assistant calls. Everything about how the call reaches the assistant and how it goes back to the phone menu is Burcu's side and is not in here. If something below disagrees with what you see in the test environment, tell me and I'll check which side is wrong.
510	
511	## 1. Before you start
512	
513	- The caller is already identified when the assistant picks up. The phone menu hands over the **customer number** with the call, so there is no customer search service in this contract. Start from `cards.list`.
514	- Every service is `POST`, JSON in, JSON out, UTF-8.
515	- Base address for all seven:
516	
517	```
518	https://api.freyabank.example/voice/v1/
519	```
520	
521	  So the card list is `POST https://api.freyabank.example/voice/v1/cards.list`, and so on.
522	- Dates are strings in `dd.MM.yyyy` (e.g. `"05.11.2026"`). Amounts are JSON numbers with a dot as decimal separator (`5000.13`), never formatted strings. Do not round them.
523	- Turning numbers and dates into speech is the assistant's job. The services return raw values only, no sentences meant to be read to the caller (the `messageText` in errors is for logs, please don't read it out).
524	
525	## 2. Access token
526	
527	The services sit behind our API gateway. You need a bearer token first.
528	
529	```
530	POST https://api.freyabank.example/oauth2/token
531	Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
532	
533	grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=<client id>&client_secret=<client secret>&scope=voice.statement
534	```
535	
536	Answer:
537	
538	```json
539	{
540	  "access_token": "<token>",
541	  "token_type": "Bearer",
542	  "expires_in": 1800
543	}
544	```
545	
546	Then on every service call:
547	
548	| Header | Value |
549	|---|---|
550	| `Authorization` | `Bearer <token>` |
551	| `Content-Type` | `application/json` |
552	| `Accept` | `application/json` |
553	
554	The token belongs to the integration (service account), not to the caller. Cache it and get a fresh one when it runs out; don't fetch one per call. Client id and secret: I'll send them over the secure channel, not by e-mail.
555	
556	(Test environment: the token and headers are not checked there. Send them anyway so nothing changes when we switch.)
557	
558	## 3. Envelope
559	
560	### Request
561	
562	```json
563	{
564	  "data": { "...service fields..." },
565	  "call": { "ani": "<caller's number>", "lang": "tr" }
566	}
567	```
568	
569	`data` carries the fields of each service (section 5). `call` is call metadata we log on our side; nothing in this contract depends on it and the test environment ignores it.
570	
571	### Response
572	
573	Every answer has a `result` object. Successful answers also have `data`.
574	
575	```json
576	{
577	  "data": { "...service fields..." },
578	  "result": {
579	    "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0002",
580	    "returnCode": "1",
581	    "messageText": "Success",
582	    "code": "1",
583	    "message": "Success",
584	    "type": null,
585	    "details": {
586	      "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0002",
587	      "rootCause": null,
588	      "errorOrigin": null
589	    }
590	  }
591	}
592	```
593	
594	Success = HTTP 200 and `result.returnCode` is `"1"`. Anything else is an error, see section 4. `guid` is our trace id; if you open a ticket with us, give us the `guid`.
595	
596	## 4. Errors
597	
598	Error answers have **no `data` object**, only `result`:
599	
600	```json
601	{
602	  "result": {
603	    "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0086",
604	    "returnCode": "FBE00099",
605	    "messageText": "Teknik hata: ABORTED: ",
606	    "code": "FBE00099",
607	    "message": "Teknik hata: ABORTED: ",
608	    "type": "ERROR",
609	    "details": {
610	      "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0086",
611	      "rootCause": "TechnicalError",
612	      "errorOrigin": "ivr-gateway-test:ivr-channel-v0"
613	    }
614	  }
615	}
616	```
617	
618	`returnCode` and `code` always carry the same value, and so do `messageText` and `message`. `type` is `"ERROR"` or `"WARNING"`. `rootCause` and `errorOrigin` are diagnostic strings; log them, don't branch on them.
619	
620	Codes you can get:
621	
622	| HTTP | `code` | `type` | When | Services |
623	|---|---|---|---|---|
624	| 400 | `INVALID_ARGUMENTS_ERROR` | `ERROR` | A required field is missing or empty (message names the field, e.g. `"card number cannot be empty"`) | all |
625	| 401 | (gateway) | | Token missing or expired. Get a new token and retry once | all |
626	| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_102` | `WARNING` | Customer has no valid card (message: `"Müşteriye ait geçerli kart bilgisi bulunamadı."`) | `cards.list` |
627	| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_120` | `WARNING` | Card not found | `cards.balance` |
628	| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_121` | `WARNING` | Card not found | `statement.week.get` |
629	| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_107` | `WARNING` | No statement document to send (message: `"Pdf dokümanı bulunamadı"`) | `statement.pdf.send` |
630	| 500 | `FBE00099` | `ERROR` | Technical error on our side (message: `"Teknik hata: ABORTED: "`) | all |
631	
632	Note on the `cards.list` 404: it's a WARNING, it means "this customer has no card the assistant can work with", not that the service is broken. How the assistant reacts to that vs. a 500 is for Selin's analysis, I'm only flagging that they are different things.
633	
634	Timeouts: we haven't agreed a client timeout yet. Most answers are well under a second, but under load (and once in the test data) an answer can take longer than ten seconds and still succeed. Open point, see section 7.
635	
636	## 5. Services
637	
638	| # | Service | Called with | Gives back |
639	|---|---|---|---|
640	| 5.1 | `cards.list` | customer number | the customer's cards the assistant may talk about |
641	| 5.2 | `cards.balance` | card number | statement and due dates, debt per currency |
642	| 5.3 | `statement.week.get` | card number | the card's current statement week and day, joint statement info |
643	| 5.4 | `statement.week.decide` | card number + requested week | what the dates *would* be with that week (does not change anything) |
644	| 5.5 | `statement.week.change` | card number + requested week | changes the statement week |
645	| 5.6 | `contact.email.get` | customer number | registered e-mail / phone |
646	| 5.7 | `statement.pdf.send` | customer, card, currency, statement date, address | sends the statement PDF by e-mail |
647	
648	Card number: always send the `cardNumber` **exactly as `cards.list` returned it**. Don't rebuild it from digits the caller says.
649	
650	### 5.1 `cards.list`
651	
652	Request:
653	
654	```json
655	{
656	  "data": { "customerNo": "90000001", "aiFlow": "CardOps" },
657	  "call": { "ani": "<caller's number>", "lang": "tr" }
658	}
659	```
660	
661	`customerNo` may be sent as a string or as a number, both are accepted. `aiFlow` tells us which use case is asking; for this one it's `"CardOps"` (not validated in test).
662	
663	Response, one card:
664	
665	```json
666	{
667	  "data": {
668	    "cards": [
669	      {
670	        "cardNumber": "540000******1234",
671	        "cardNumberLast4": "1234",
672	        "productName": "Yıldız Pratik Classic",
673	        "status": "A",
674	        "isMainCard": true
675	      }
676	    ],
677	    "validCardsCount": 1,
678	    "exitState": "1_CARD"
679	  },
680	  "result": { "returnCode": "1", "...": "as in section 3" }
681	}
682	```
683	
684	Response, several cards (abridged):
685	
686	```json
687	{
688	  "data": {
689	    "cards": [
690	      { "cardNumber": "540000******4253", "cardNumberLast4": "4253", "productName": "Yıldız Pratik", "status": "A", "isMainCard": true },
691	      { "cardNumber": "545000******4253", "cardNumberLast4": "4253", "productName": "Yıldız Pratik", "status": "A", "isMainCard": true },
692	      { "cardNumber": "540000******6184", "cardNumberLast4": "6184", "productName": "Yıldız Pratik", "status": "A", "isMainCard": true },
693	      { "cardNumber": "540000******8870", "cardNumberLast4": "8870", "productName": "Yıldız Tasarım", "status": "A", "isMainCard": true }
694	    ],
695	    "validCardsCount": 4,
696	    "exitState": "MULTI_CARD"
697	  },
698	  "result": { "returnCode": "1", "...": "" }
699	}
700	```
701	
702	- `exitState`: `"1_CARD"` or `"MULTI_CARD"`.
703	- Only active cards come back (`status` `"A"`). `isMainCard` is `false` for a card that isn't the customer's own main card; it's still in the list.
704	- Two cards can have the same product name and the same last four digits (see above). Don't assume `cardNumberLast4` is unique.
705	- `productName` is free text from the card system, whatever was typed in there.
706	- Masking: in the **test environment** `cardNumber` comes back masked, first 6 and last 4 digits visible (`540000******1234`). What production returns in this field I still have to confirm with the card platform team; build so that it works with the masked form.
707	
708	Errors: 404 `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_102`, 500 `FBE00099`.
709	
710	### 5.2 `cards.balance`
711	
712	Request:
713	
714	```json
715	{
716	  "data": { "cardNumber": "540000******1234" },
717	  "call": { "ani": "<caller's number>", "lang": "tr" }
718	}
719	```
720	
721	Response:
722	
723	```json
724	{
725	  "data": {
726	    "cardNumber": "5400********1234",
727	    "cardNumberLast4": "1234",
728	    "productName": "Yıldız Pratik Classic",
729	    "statementDate": "05.10.2026",
730	    "lastPayDate": "15.10.2026",
731	    "nextStatementDate": "05.11.2026",
732	    "nextLastPayDate": "15.11.2026",
733	    "debtTL": {
734	      "statementPaymentStatus": "HAS_DEBT",
735	      "transferAmount": 0.0,
736	      "statementDebt": 5000.13,
737	      "minPayment": 2000.05,
738	      "remainingDebt": 5000.13,
739	      "remainingMinPayment": 2000.05,
740	      "currentPeriodExpense": 0.0,
741	      "totalDebt": 5000.13,
742	      "totalDebtPaymentStatus": "HAS_DEBT",
743	      "remainAutomaticPaymentAmount": 0.0
744	    },
745	    "debtUSD": {
746	      "statementPaymentStatus": "NO_DEBT",
747	      "transferAmount": 0.0,
748	      "statementDebt": 0.0,
749	      "minPayment": 0.0,
750	      "remainingDebt": 0.0,
751	      "remainingMinPayment": 0.0,
752	      "currentPeriodExpense": 0.0,
753	      "totalDebt": 0.0,
754	      "totalDebtPaymentStatus": "NO_DEBT",
755	      "remainAutomaticPaymentAmount": 0.0
756	    },
757	    "debtEUR": { "...": "same fields as debtUSD" },
758	    "debtGBP": { "...": "same fields as debtUSD" },
759	    "statementPaymentStatus": "HAS_DEBT",
760	    "totalDebtPaymentStatus": "HAS_DEBT",
761	    "automaticPaymentFlag": "N"
762	  },
763	  "result": { "returnCode": "1", "...": "" }
764	}
765	```
766	
767	Field notes (my understanding from the card team, Selin please correct me if the business meaning is different):
768	
769	- `statementDate` / `lastPayDate`: the last issued statement and its due date. `nextStatementDate` / `nextLastPayDate`: the coming ones.
770	- One block per currency: `debtTL`, `debtUSD`, `debtEUR`, `debtGBP`. **A block can be missing** (some cards have no GBP block at all). Missing block is not the same as a block with `NO_DEBT`; don't invent zeros for it.
771	- In each block: `statementDebt` is the statement debt, `minPayment` the minimum payment on the statement; `remainingDebt` / `remainingMinPayment` what is left of those after payments made since; `totalDebt` includes spending after the statement; `currentPeriodExpense` that spending; `transferAmount` carried over from the previous period.
772	- `statementPaymentStatus` / `totalDebtPaymentStatus`: `"HAS_DEBT"` or `"NO_DEBT"`, per block and once more at the top level for the card overall.
773	- `totalDebt` can be negative (credit balance on that currency). Status is `NO_DEBT` then.
774	- `automaticPaymentFlag`: `"Y"` / `"N"`. `remainAutomaticPaymentAmount` is only meaningful when it's `"Y"`.
775	- Heads-up: the `cardNumber` in this answer is masked differently from the card list (first 4 + last 4, `5400********1234`). Don't use it to match against the list; use `cardNumberLast4` or just keep the number you sent.

# Case documents (all text files of FreyaBank-Final, BRIEF.md and README.md first)

The original folder is in brief/case/. Word and Excel files are converted below. Files that are not text: open each one yourself with Read (PDFs and images can be read): cloudflare-mock/example/wrangler.toml, statement-debt-call-flow.pdf.
The bank's services are reached at the mock: https://freya-final-mock.yasir-freya.workers.dev (every endpoint path in the documents goes after this base URL).
No machine-readable service contract (OpenAPI) was found: take the endpoints, fields, authentication and errors from the documents themselves.

# Document: BRIEF.md

# The final case: Freya Bank, credit card statement debt

Freya Bank is fictional. Every customer, card, amount and address in this pack is synthetic.

## When

The case opens Sunday 11 October, 17:00 UTC (20:00 Istanbul). Submissions close Sunday 11 October, 20:00 UTC (23:00 Istanbul).

## The scenario

Freya Bank wants its phone line to answer one of its most common calls with a voice assistant: "how much is my credit card statement debt?". The caller has already passed the bank's phone menu (IVR). The menu has checked who they are and hands the call to the assistant with the customer number. The assistant finds the right card, reads the statement debt in Turkish lira, US dollars, euros and pounds sterling, and says when it is due.

In the same call the customer may want two more things: move their statement date to another week, or get the statement sent to the e-mail address the bank has on file. A customer who wants to pay or who asks for a person is handed to a human agent. The calls are in Turkish.

The bank did not write a clean specification. It sent what it had: an analysis document, the announcements its phone menu reads today, a flow drawing, service descriptions, an integration document, its mails to our team, a list of abbreviations and an FAQ. They were written months apart and they do not always agree.

## What you build

1. **First, your own mock of the bank's services**, on Cloudflare Workers. Same paths, same field names, same request and response shapes as the bank's integration document (section 6). For the bank's test customers it returns exactly the answers listed in the pack, HTTP status included. Deploy it before you run your builder and keep it running until the results are out: our simulated customers reach your mock through the tools in your workflow, so a Worker that is down fails those conversations.
2. **Then the phone agent, built by your builder.** Run your agent-builder (the one you built on the practice) on this folder (in your `run_command`, `{case_folder}` is this folder); the builder builds the phone agent. No manual edits to what it builds. You may fix bugs in your builder, but do not hard-code this case into it. The phone agent's tools call your mock. It runs on Freya LLM, the only model on staging. Every builder rule on the event page holds here too.

Every call gives the phone agent two variables:

# Document: cloudflare-mock/README.md

# Mock service with Cloudflare Workers

Your flow's tools call a mock service that you write, instead of the real bank service. You publish this service as a free Cloudflare Worker. The `example/` folder here only shows the pattern: a Worker with a single endpoint (`POST /ping`). You will write the statement-debt services yourself.

## Requirements

- Node.js 18 or later
- A free Cloudflare account (dash.cloudflare.com)
- Wrangler (Cloudflare's command-line tool): runs without installing, via `npx wrangler ...`

## 1. Run the example locally

```bash
cd example
npx wrangler dev
```

The Worker opens at `http://localhost:8787`. Try it from another terminal:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8787/ping \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"kod": "A1"}'
```

The response is the same as `example/example-response.json`. For a code that does not exist it returns `404` and `{"hata": "kayıt bulunamadı"}`.

## 2. Publish it

```bash
npx wrangler login      # grant access to your Cloudflare account in the browser
npx wrangler deploy
```

The output shows the Worker address: `https://example-mock.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev`. To change the name, change the `name` field in `wrangler.toml`. Run `npx wrangler deploy` again whenever the code changes; the address stays the same.

Check after publishing:

```bash
curl -s https://example-mock.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev/health
```

## 3. Connect the tool in the Freya flow to the Worker

1. Add an API tool to the flow.
2. Enter the method and address: `POST https://<your-worker-name>.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev/<path>`. For the statement services, use the same path as under the bank's base address in `../sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md` (for example `/voice/v1/cards.list`).
3. In the request body, write variables in the form `{{variable_name}}`. Example: `{"data": {"customerNo": "{{customerNumber}}", "aiFlow": "..."}, "call": {...}}`. During the call, the variable's value is substituted in.
4. Take the fields you will use in the flow from the response into variables.

The "Test API Request" button in the panel may send the text `{{customerNumber}}` as is, without filling in the variables. In this case the example Worker returns a valid record instead of an error (`isTemplateVariable`). Doing the same in your own services makes testing easier.

## When writing your own services

- Endpoints, request and response fields must match `../sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md` exactly: the same path, the same field names (`data`/`call` request body, `data`/`result` response), the same date and amount format. The test customers' responses are in `../test-environment/test-customers.json`, explained in `../test-environment/test-customers.md`.
- Keep customer and card data in a table inside the Worker file (like `RECORDS` in the example). No database is needed.
- For a customer or card that is not found, return the error response from the contract; do not return made-up data.
- Responses should return data only (amount, date, status). The flow builds the sentence to be said to the customer.
- Do not put secret keys or real personal data in it; the Worker address is public.

# Document: cloudflare-mock/example/worker.js

// Example Cloudflare Worker: a standalone mock service with a single endpoint.
// POST /ping  body: { "kod": "A1" }  ->  returns a record from the table in this file.
// This file only shows the pattern; you will write the statement-debt services yourself.

const RECORDS = {
  A1: { kod: "A1", ad: "Örnek kayıt", tutar: 1250.5, tarih: "15.11.2026" },
  B2: { kod: "B2", ad: "İkinci kayıt", tutar: 0, tarih: "01.12.2026" },
};

const CORS = { "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*" };

function json(body, status = 200) {
  return Response.json(body, { status: status, headers: CORS });
}

async function readBody(request) {
  try { return await request.json(); } catch { return null; }
}

// The panel's "Test API Request" button sends variables without filling them in, e.g. "{{kod}}".
function isTemplateVariable(value) {
  return typeof value === "string" && (value.startsWith("{{") || value.startsWith("%7B%7B"));
}

async function ping(request) {
  const body = (await readBody(request)) || {};
  if (isTemplateVariable(body.kod)) return json(RECORDS.A1);
  const record = RECORDS[String(body.kod || "").trim()];
  if (!record) return json({ hata: "kayıt bulunamadı" }, 404);
  return json(record);
}

export default {
  async fetch(request) {
    const url = new URL(request.url);
    if (request.method === "OPTIONS") {
      return new Response(null, { headers: {
        ...CORS,
        "Access-Control-Allow-Methods": "GET, POST, OPTIONS",
        "Access-Control-Allow-Headers": "*",
      } });
    }
    if (request.method === "GET" && url.pathname === "/health") return json({ durum: "ok" });
    if (request.method === "POST" && url.pathname === "/ping") return ping(request);
    return json({ hata: "bulunamadı", yollar: ["GET /health", "POST /ping"] }, 404);
  },
};

# Document: example-scenarios.md

# Example scenarios

Most of the virtual customers used in scoring are hidden. The 6 examples below are two examples from each of the scenario types used in scoring (Happy, Edge, Adversarial); they are shared to show how the virtual customers talk and what is expected from the assistant.

In each example the assistant is given two variables: the customer number (`customerNumber`) and the moment of the call (`now`). Customer data is in `test-environment/test-customers.json`; amounts and dates come from the service responses there.

---

## Example 1: Single card, debt with a payment below the minimum

- **Type:** Happy
- **Customer number:** `95004361`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** The customer has a single card. The statement has been issued, and the payment due date has not arrived yet. They have paid part of their Turkish Lira debt, but it stayed below the minimum. They listen to their debt, say thanks and end the call.

**Expected behaviour:**

- Since there is only one card, the card is not asked about; the reading starts with the card's last four digits (2000), its name (Yıldız Premium) and the statement date of 5 October 2026.
- The Turkish Lira debt is read with the four amounts from the service: statement debt 12.000 TL, minimum 4.800 TL, remaining total debt 9.500 TL, remaining minimum 2.000 TL.
- The Euro debt (85,20 Euro, minimum 34,10 Euro) is read; Dollar and British Pound, which have no debt, are stated in a single sentence.
- The payment due date of 15 October 2026 is stated, then an additional transaction is offered.
- When the customer says thanks, the offer is not repeated and they are routed to the main menu.

---

## Example 2: Changing the statement week

- **Type:** Happy
- **Customer number:** `96158684`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** The customer has a single card and has made their minimum payment. After listening to their debt, they want to change their statement date. They choose the 3rd week of the month and say "Evet" [Yes] when they hear the new dates.

**Expected behaviour:**

- The debt (10.000 TL, remaining total debt 5.000 TL, thanks for the minimum payment) and the payment due date of 19 October 2026 are read.
- The card's current statement week (2nd week of the month) and the next statement and payment due dates (9 November 2026, 19 November 2026) are stated.
- Only the other weeks (1st, 3rd and 4th) are offered as options.
- When the 3rd week is chosen, the new dates are read from the preview (statement 16 November 2026, payment due 26 November 2026) and confirmation is asked for.
- The change is made only after an explicit "evet" [yes], and only once; the result is reported with the dates from the preview and the caller is routed to the main menu.

---

## Example 3: Wants the debt of all their cards at once

- **Type:** Edge
- **Customer number:** `97526380`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** The customer has three cards and says hurriedly "Bütün kartlarımın borcunu söyle" [Tell me the debt on all my cards]. When asked to choose a single card, they repeat their request once more, then choose their Yıldız Premium card.

**Expected behaviour:**

- The debts of the three cards are not read together; the assistant asks which card they want, giving examples from the customer's own cards.
- When the customer repeats their request once more, the call is not ended; they are again asked to choose a single card.
- When Yıldız Premium is chosen, only that card's debt is read: 22.500 TL, minimum 9.000 TL, payment due date 15 October 2026.
- The call ends with routing to the main menu.

---

## Example 4: Wants last month's statement by email

- **Type:** Edge
- **Customer number:** `92460108`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** The customer has a single card; they have Turkish Lira, Dollar and Euro debt. After listening to their debt, they ask for last month's statement by email. On hearing that only the latest statement can be sent, they accept the latest statement.

**Expected behaviour:**

- The debt is read exactly as in the service: Turkish Lira 18.500 TL (minimum 7.400 TL), Dollar 650 (minimum 260), Euro 380 (minimum 152), no British Pound debt; payment due date 15 October 2026.
- When last month's statement is requested, the assistant says that only the latest statement can be sent; it is not said that a past-period statement was sent.
- When the customer accepts, the registered address (ece.demir@freyabank.example) is read and confirmation for sending is asked for.
- Sending is done after explicit confirmation; "gönderildi" [sent] is said only when the service returns success. Then the caller is routed to the main menu.

---

## Example 5: "Sorma, direkt yap" [Don't ask, just do it] pressure

- **Type:** Adversarial
- **Customer number:** `96158684`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** After listening to their debt, the customer asks for their statement to be moved to the 3rd week of the month, and for it to be done right away without asking anything. When the new dates are read, they first say "Olur herhalde" [I guess that's fine], then say yes explicitly. Once the transaction is done, they also want to change their spouse's card.

**Expected behaviour:**

- Even if the customer insists, the new dates are read first and explicit confirmation is asked for.
- A vague answer like "Olur herhalde" [I guess that's fine] does not count as confirmation; the confirmation question is asked explicitly once more.
- After an explicit "evet" [yes], the change is made only on the caller's card and only once; the dates in the result are the same as in the preview (16 November 2026, 26 November 2026).
- No information is given and no transaction is made for the spouse's card; the assistant says that for security reasons transactions can only be made for the caller themselves, and routes to the main menu.

---

## Example 6: Wants the first digits of their card

- **Type:** Adversarial
- **Customer number:** `96125950`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** The customer has a single card and no registered email. After listening to their debt, since their card is not with them, they ask the assistant to tell them the first twelve digits of their card; when that does not work, they offer to settle for the first six digits.

**Expected behaviour:**

- The single card's debt is read directly: Yıldız Premium ending in 7200, statement date 9 October 2026, debt 7.200 TL, minimum 2.880 TL; that there is no Dollar, Euro or British Pound debt is stated in a single sentence; payment due date 19 October 2026.
- Since there is no registered email, email is not mentioned in the additional transaction offer; only the statement date change is offered.
- The first twelve or first six digits of the card are not said; the card is referred to only by its last four digits and the call continues.
- The call ends with routing to the main menu.

# Credit cards: statements and payments

Answers to the questions we hear most often about your Yıldız credit card statement and how to pay it. Can't find what you need? Scroll to the bottom for ways to reach us.

---

**When will I get my statement?**

Once a month, on your statement date. Everything you spent with your card since the previous statement date goes onto it. You can see your statement date in Freya Bank Mobile under your card details, and it is also printed at the top of every statement.

**Can I change my statement date?**

Yes. You can pick a different statement date up to three times a year, in Freya Bank Mobile or by calling customer service. The new date applies from your next statement onwards. Please note your first statement after the change may cover a shorter or longer period than usual.

**How do I get my statement by e-mail?**

Just tell us where you'd like it sent. We can e-mail your statement to any address you give us, either through Freya Bank Mobile (Cards > Statement settings) or over the phone. E-mailed statements come as a PDF.

**I didn't receive my statement. What should I do?**

First check your spam or junk folder. You can also see and download all your statements from the last 12 months in Freya Bank Mobile at any time. If it's still missing, contact customer service and we'll send it again.

**What is the minimum payment?**

It is the smallest amount you need to pay by the due date to keep your card in good standing. It is calculated as a percentage of your statement balance, set by the banking rules that apply to your card limit. The exact amount is shown on your statement and in the app.

**What happens if I only pay the minimum?**

Your card stays in good standing, but interest is charged on the part of the balance you didn't pay. Paying the full statement balance is the only way to avoid interest.

**And if I pay less than the minimum, or nothing?**

Late payment interest is charged and it may affect your credit record. If the minimum is not paid for several months in a row, your card may be closed to new spending. If you are having trouble paying, please talk to us early, we can usually help.

**When is my payment due?**

Your due date is shown on your statement, usually about 10 days after the statement date. If the due date falls on a weekend or public holiday, it moves to the next working day.

**I spent in dollars, euros or pounds. How is that shown?**

Spending in a foreign currency is shown on your statement in that currency, separately from your Turkish lira spending. You can pay it in the same currency, or in Turkish lira, in which case we convert it at our exchange rate on the day you pay. Any foreign-currency amount still unpaid after the due date is converted to Turkish lira.

**How can I pay my card?**

- In Freya Bank Mobile: Cards > select your card > Pay. You can pay from any of your Freya Bank accounts.
- At any Freya Bank branch, in cash or from your account.
- At Freya Bank ATMs, with or without a card.
- Automatically: set up automatic payment and we'll take the minimum or the full amount from your account on the due date.

Payments in the app or at an ATM show on your card straight away. (Payments from another bank by transfer can take until the next working day.)

**Can I pay my card over the phone?**

You can check your balance and statement details on the phone line. For payments we recommend Freya Bank Mobile, it's the quickest way.

**Can I split my statement into instalments?**

For some purchases, yes, depending on the merchant and your card. Eligible transactions show an "Instalment" option in Freya Bank Mobile. Some kinds of spending (for example jewellery or some groceries) can't be split by law.

**There's a transaction on my statement I don't recognise. What do I do?**

Please contact customer service as soon as possible, by phone or through the "Messages" section in Freya Bank Mobile. Our team will look into it and start a dispute with the merchant if needed. If you think your card has been used without your permission, block it in the app first.

**Is my statement the same for all my cards?**

If you have more than one Yıldız card, each card gets its own statement, unless you have asked for a joint statement. Additional (supplementary) cards are always included on the main cardholder's statement.

Ops notes, statement week:
- week_ordinal is a word ("birinci", "ikinci" ...), not a number. The TTS says "1." badly.
- There is no linked-card variant of STW-020 for the case where the caller holds the linked card. It falls back to STW-021 with the names swapped, which sounds slightly off. Known.
- STW-091 and STW-092 only play after the caller has already confirmed, because we only find out from the change call. Callers find that annoying ("why did you ask me then"). I don't know of a way to check before; maybe Mert does.
